messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High 5xx rate observed from NLB -> Envoy mesh in eu-central-1 (az-b). Service: public-ingress. Start: 2026-03-15T09:12:34Z. Threshold breached: 5xx > 15% for 5m. Paging @sre-julia @oncall-sre
sre-julia: Ack. jumping in — investigating routing + envoy upstream health. Can someone grab customer impact?

emma: Seeing the alerts in support dashboard. ~120 errors/min across EU region, ~30% of prod requests failing for a subset of customers (PLG onboarding traffic). No billing impact but UX broken. Customers on eu cluster most affected.

raj: I see Envoy 503 counter spike on the frontend pods in az-b. Upstream target group for gw-alb-euc1b shows healthy targets but connection resets rising. Possible TCP RSTs from nodes.

max: I'm pulling k8s and ELB metrics now. Quick check: `kubectl -n infra exec -it envoy-frontend-3 -- curl localhost:9901/stats | grep upstream_cx_` returned huge `upstream_cx_connect_fail` and `upstream_rq_5xx`.

raj: Copy those stats. Pasting snippets: ```
upstream_cx_connect_fail: 4231
upstream_rq_5xx: 5120
upstream_cx_total: 12000
```

sre-julia: Those connect_fail numbers look like backend nodes dropping connections. Are there any recent deploys? eng-releases shows none for the frontends in last 12h.

ops-bot: Deploy: none. ASG scaling event 2026-03-15T08:50Z in eu-central-1b due to CPU surge; several nodes replaced (auto-replace).

max: The replaced nodes show kernel messages with `TCP: RST due to conntrack overflow` on some node logs. Might be conntrack exhaustion after a brief spike.

emma: Support is getting a handful of angry messages. One customer (acct-9321) reported app failing to load on EU region. Escalated to account team.

raj: Immediate mitigation options: 1) weight shift traffic away from az-b to az-a/c via Route 53 weighted DNS or ALB target group weights; 2) scale up target group capacity in eu-central-1a/c; 3) temporarily reduce keepalive/connection pooling to reduce conntrack pressure.

sre-julia: Prefer quick weight shift + safe autoscale. Max, can you trigger a weight shift at ALB level? Raj, can you draft a temporary keepalive change we can roll (and rollback)? Emma, update customers with ETA 15-30m.

max: Doing ALB weight change now — moving 40% traffic off az-b to az-a and az-c. Using CLI: ```
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:... --default-actions '[{"type":"forward","forwardConfig":{"targetGroups":[{"targetGroupArn":"tg-a","weight":45},{"targetGroupArn":"tg-c","weight":45},{"targetGroupArn":"tg-b","weight":10}]}}]'
```

ops-bot: ALB weight change applied. New weights 45/10/45 (a/b/c). Propagation observed within ~30s.

raj: Rolling change to envoy keepalive config suggestion: tweak `upstream.connection_idle_timeout` from 300s -> 60s and reduce `max_conn` per host to ease conntrack. I can produce a canary patch for two frontend replicas. Suggest canary 10% traffic first.

sre-julia: Do canary patch on 2 pods in az-a only. If stable for 5m, roll more. Provide kubectl command.

raj: Applying canary config via configmap update: ```
kubectl -n infra apply -f envoy-keepalive-canary.yaml
# envoy-keepalive-canary.yaml contains reduced keepalive + conn limits
```

max: Watchdog: envoy metrics show 5xx dropping immediately after weight change: `upstream_rq_5xx` rate reduced to ~900/min from 5k/min. We'll keep an eye on conntrack errors.

emma: Customer msg: "We're seeing errors but platform team is working on it. Expect improvement in 15-30m." Posted to affected customers list.

support-liaison: Logging a customer-impact ticket and adding affected account IDs. Notifying enterprise CS.

ops-bot: Node logs: conntrack entries peaked ~450k on replaced nodes (threshold 262k). Kernel OOM not observed.

raj: Looks like conntrack table size on some nodes was set low — `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` shows 262144 on older instances; autoscaled ones had a default of 131072. We'll standardize later. For now weight shift + keepalive change is mitigating.

sre-julia: Agreed. Next steps: 1) finish canary roll for keepalive across eu frontends if metrics look stable; 2) increase conntrack limit on pool via user-data patch and trigger replacement or live sysctl bump where possible; 3) open incident for postmortem. Who owns conntrack change?

max: I'll coordinate conntrack sysctl bump and schedule a rolling restart of the nodes with updated AMI or cloud-init. For immediate relief I'm bumping via SSM on healthy nodes: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` — applying to non-terminated nodes now.

ops-bot: SSM run command completed on 8/12 nodes in eu-central-1. New value 524288 applied. Remaining nodes are being drained/replaced by ASG.

raj: Canary keepalive roll completed — no increase in 5xx for 10m now. Proceed to roll to remaining frontends with 50% rollout steps.

max: Rolling ahead with conntrack bump on remaining nodes during drain windows to avoid client disruption.

sre-julia: Monitoring: looking good. 5xx rate back to baseline ~0.5%. Latency stable. Marking incident as mitigated.

emma: Notifying customers: "Issue mitigated; engineering applied routing and network config changes. Full postmortem forthcoming."

support-liaison: Created incident ticket INC-2026-348 with impacted accounts + timeline.

oncall-bot: Incident status -> MITIGATED at 2026-03-15T09:37:11Z. Summary: Envoy upstream connection failures due to conntrack exhaustion after ASG replacement; mitigated by ALB weight shift, envoy keepalive tuning, and conntrack limit bump. Postmortem owner: @raj.

sre-julia: I'll schedule a short blameless postmortem doc and link the runbooks: runbook/networking/conntrack and runbook/loadbalancer/weight-shift. Also recommend automated conntrack alarms and node userdata check in ASG.

raj: I'll own the postmortem and follow-up action items: AMI update, ASG lifecycle hook to set conntrack, and revisit default keepalive/conn settings and testing.

max: Filing follow-up PR to infra repo to set nf_conntrack_max via cloud-init and add unit tests.

emma: Closing customer comms loop. Thanks all. :thumbsup: 

sre-julia: Good job team. Leaving handoff note for next oncall: observe eu-central-1 for 2h and watch `upstream_cx_connect_fail`, `conntrack_count`, and 5xx alerts.

support-liaison: Handoff accepted by next oncall.

oncall-bot: Handoff posted to #oncall-handoff.

sre-julia: Filing post-incident task list now.

-- end of thread --
